snippet.title: Thailand's SUGAR TREES / Escape from Bangkok to Phetchaburi / Motorbike Tour 2026
snippet.description:
Welcome to Phetchaburi, a province of thailand that can surprise absolutely anybody! 

Today we're exploring Phetchaburi Province, located in just 2 hours drive from Bangkok. A province that 98% of people simply skip on their way to southern Thailand, however there's so much to see here!

In today's travel video we are going to visit local sugar palm orchard to know more about natural sugar production in Thailand and to try one of the most amazing desserts in the country. Today we will be exploring the most unusual caves with temples inside, enjoying delicious local Thai food, taking a stroll along a walking street with street food and many other things!
Let's enjoy one of the most fantastic provinces of Thailand which is located so close to Bangkok!

snippet.title: THE HARSH TRUTH About Dating a Broke Woman 🇵🇭
snippet.description:
Most men who fly into the Philippines think they understand the culture… until they date a woman who’s living in pure survival mode.
This isn’t the West. There’s no government safety net. No child support system. No monthly assistance.
Here? Family comes first. Survival comes first. Reality comes first.

And if you’re a Western man dating in the Philippines, you need to understand exactly what that means.
Not to judge it — but to respect it.

In this video, I break down the real cultural forces men never see coming:
• why “broke” does NOT mean “lazy” here
• why survival shapes relationships
• why family obligations matter more than romance
• why Western men misread Filipino intentions
• why some women ask for support — and why it isn’t “gold digging”
• how to spot the difference between authentic and opportunistic
• the truth about love, loyalty, and responsibility in Filipino culture

This is not an attack.
This is Asian reality — seen through boots on the ground.

If you come here searching for beauty or youth, but you don’t understand the weight these women carry…
You’re not dating.
You’re playing with someone’s survival.

And in the Philippines, survival is not a game.

Welcome to Asia Uncovered — where the truth hits harder than the fantasy ever could.

snippet.title: Permaculture and the Khok Nong Na Model of Thailand
snippet.description:
Join Chris on a journey through the lush landscapes of Thailand as he delves into the world of permaculture and explores the sustainable farming practices of the Khok Nong Na model (โคกหนองนาโมเดล). From the sandy beaches of the south to the verdant fields of Sisaket province, learn how the principles of permaculture intertwine with the age-old wisdom of Thai farming.

In this video:
🌱 Discover the essence of permaculture and its permanent agriculture goals.
🌏 Learn about the Khok Nong Na model, a sustainable farming initiative promoted by the Thai monarchy.
🌳 Watch as Chris shares his personal transition from the scuba-diving world to becoming an eco-conscious farmer.
🍌 Get hands-on tips about planting bananas and understanding their unique biology.
💡 Hear Chris's call for knowledge-sharing, collaboration, and community building in the world of eco-farming.

Whether you're an eco-enthusiast, a beginner in farming, or someone curious about sustainable living, this video offers a fresh perspective on harmonizing with nature while building a sustainable future.

snippet.title: 🇵🇭 IF YOU ARRIVE BROKE IN THE PHILIPPINES — THIS HAPPENS FAST
snippet.description:
Most foreign men don’t realize this before arriving in the Philippines.

They land expecting opportunity, connection, and a fresh start — but without financial preparation, the experience quickly changes.

This video was filmed in Manila and explains the reality many Western men only discover after they get here.

Relationships anywhere in the world involve exchange.
In Southeast Asia, that exchange becomes visible very quickly if you arrive unprepared.

A young woman brings youth, beauty, energy, and time.
A grown man brings stability, leadership, and direction.

When one side shows up without their part of the equation, expectations collapse fast.

This isn’t about judgment.
It’s about understanding the environment before you step into it.

If you’re planning to visit the Philippines — especially Manila or Angeles City — this is something every man should hear before booking a flight.

Because preparation protects you.

This is Asia Uncovered — where the truth hits harder than the fantasy you came here chasing.

snippet.title: I Found a Secret Kingdom of Permaculture
snippet.description:
In November 2026, join the International Permaculture Convergence (IPC16) at Wisdom King Farm! This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to bridge the gap between Western Permaculture and Thailand's local wisdom.

👉 Sign up for the mailing list & event updates here: https://thaipermaculture.org/events/ipc16/

🚜 SUPPORT THESE STORIES:
Documenting the hidden agricultural gems of Thailand and telling theese stories takes time, travel, and resources. If you value this content and want to help share more of these stories, please consider supporting the channel directly:

👉 Join the Patreon Community: https://www.patreon.com/FarangFarm

What is Permaculture?

It sounds like a simple question, but for the last five years living on my own farm in Isaan, I’ve struggled to give it a clear answer.

In this episode, we travel to the outskirts of Bangkok to visit one of the most spectacular, and surprising, locations I have ever seen: The Golden Jubilee Museum of Agriculture, also known as Wisdom King Farm.

What looks like a futuristic set of golden pyramids is actually the beating heart of Thailand’s agricultural resistance. We were there on a high-stakes mission with the Thai Permaculture Network to negotiate a partnership for the upcoming IPC16. The goal? To bring the global permaculture movement to Thailand and merge it with the country's own powerful philosophy.

The King’s Philosophy and Permaculture:

For decades, King Bhumibol Adulyadej (Rama 9) championed a system remarkably similar to permaculture, known as the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (SEP). Through his "New Theory Agriculture" and the Khok Nong Na Model, he provided a blueprint for farmers to survive economic crises and climate change.

The model uses a specific land design ratio to ensure food security and water management. But as we explore the museum, we learn that this isn't just a rigid set of rules; it is a conscious design process driven by ethics.

The International Permaculture Convergence:

This video is an invitation. We successfully negotiated with the museum and the Thai Farmer’s Network to co-host the next International Permaculture convergence. They agreed, but with one condition: we had to extend the event to give the local Thai farmers a full day to showcase their wisdom.

From 3D cinemas teaching soil biology to "Fair Share" dormitories that test your commitment to community living, this place is a fortress of knowledge. Whether you call it Permaculture, Wanakaset (Forest Farming), or Sufficiency Economy, the goal is the same: designing a future where we don't just survive, but thrive.

The "new normal" of burning seasons and industrial farming isn't working. It is time to design a new future. We hope you will join us in Thailand to be a part of it.

snippet.title: 9 WORST Tips for a Road Trip From Thailand!
snippet.description:
Can you do Laos' famous Bolaven Loop by car? Is it possible to trade the rusty motorbikes for reliable air-conditioning and still capture the spirit of adventure?

We decided to find out. This is the Grown-Up's Guide to Southern Laos: a road trip from Ubon, Thailand, across the border to Pakse and beyond. We set out to create a perfect, civilized itinerary filled with Asia's most spectacular waterfalls.

Join us as we discover just how spectacularly a well-laid plan can unravel...

For years, the Bolaven Loop has been a legendary rite of passage for backpackers. But we believe travel evolves. This guide is for those who still crave discovery but prefer a comfortable bed over a hostel bunk.

OUR "GROWN-UP'S GUIDE" ITINERARY & HIGHLIGHTS:

🌏 The Border Crossing (Ubon, Thailand to Pakse, Laos):

Our journey begins in Ubon Ratchathani, Thailand. We break down the surprisingly simple process of crossing the Chong Mek border into Laos with your own vehicle. Learn from our planning on how to handle the car's 'passport', insurance, and currency exchange.

Pro-Tip: A little pre-planning makes the border crossing a breeze, setting the perfect tone for a smooth, drama-free trip!

🏞️ Pakse & The Dao Heuang Market:

Welcome to Pakse, the charming capital of Southern Laos! We dive straight into the heart of the region's culture at the Dao Heuang Market, a vibrant assault on the senses. Discover the potent smell of padaek and the fascinating mix of Thai, Lao, and French colonial influence baked into the local food and architecture.

💦 The Waterfalls of the Bolaven Loop (By Car!):

The main event! Driving the loop reveals some of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking natural wonders, all accessible without a motorbike.

Tad Fane: Home to a thunderous twin waterfall plunging into a deep gorge. For the adventurous grown-up, there's an exhilarating zipline that soars directly over the canyon, offering an unforgettable perspective.

Tad Lo: A picture-perfect cascade with a serene, influencer-approved coffee shop right at its edge. The ideal spot for a relaxing break and a stunning photo opportunity.

Pha Suam: A visit to this culturally rich waterfall park, which offers a poignant reminder that some destinations are more about the journey than the final viewpoint.

This trip was meant to be a test of an itinerary, but it quickly became a test of patience, memory, and the critical importance of travelling with someone who knows how to have fun when you've forgotten how. 

This is our road to hell... and back.

Thanks for watching.

snippet.title: The REAL Downside of Living in Rural Thailand
snippet.description:
Even when surrounded by welcoming people, the challenges of adapting to a new culture can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness. This video explores the realities of expat life in Thailand and how it can impact relationships. Discover ways to deal with feeling lonely and navigate the complexities of living abroad.

Welcome to my stand-up special, performed exclusively for an unappreciative field of insects. As it turns out, living on a beautiful farm in rural Thailand is 95% idyllic paradise and 5% spiralling into a unique brand of madness where you start critiquing the comedic timing of invertebrates. This video is about that 5%.

It's about the strange paradox of being an expat: you can be surrounded by the kindest people on the planet, yet still feel alone. It's a loneliness that doesn't come from a lack of company, but from a cultural and linguistic chasm so wide that even your best jokes fall into it and are never seen again.

One of the biggest symbols of this chasm is a single word: Farang (ฝรั่ง).
For years, some people have known my name is Chris, but to some people (not everyone), I'm still just 'the Farang'. It’s not meant to be rude, but it's a constant, gentle reminder that you’re not from around here. You're the outsider, the 'other'. In this video, I went on a historical deep-dive to find out where this word actually comes from—the journey from the Germanic 'Franks' to the Persians and finally to the stone-carved statues at Wat Pho is more bizarre than you'd think. It's a word that carries centuries of historical baggage, and sometimes, that baggage feels heavy.

When the silence gets too loud and the feeling of being a 19th-century caricature in a top hat gets a bit much, you have to find a reset button. My reset button, apparently, is a 20km pilgrimage to the fluorescent-lit sanctuary of a 7-Eleven. It’s a quest for an anchor in a sea of chaos; a predictable, air-conditioned pocket of order where the products are in perfect lines and salvation comes in the form of a processed ham and cheese toasty.

I know, I know. For a guy who champions farm-to-table living, embracing the glory of plastic-wrapped comfort food seems a little out of character. But that's the core of it—when you feel a million miles from everything you know, you don't always crave nutritious food. You crave comfort food. A little taste of the familiar to keep you grounded when everything else feels... well, foreign.

This video is an honest look at the less glamorous side of living the dream. It’s about managing the quiet moments, the mundane realities, and the crippling loneliness that can creep in on a random Tuesday. It's proof that sometimes, the most important journey you can take is the one to grab a snack.

What's your 'comfort food' when you feel far from home? Have you ever felt like an outsider in a new place? Let me know in the comments below!
And if you want to see me connect with people who actually laugh at my jokes, be sure to subscribe for more on the journey to the International Permaculture Convergence!

Either way, you needed to hear it.

snippet.title: Exploring Mall Esplanade Nonthaburi
snippet.description:
Esplanade Cineplex Ngamwongwan – Khae Rai is the main mall/shopping-and-entertainment complex commonly referred to as Mall Esplanade Nonthaburi. It’s located in Tambon Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi District, Nonthaburi 11000, Thailand on Rattanathibet Road and is part of The Esplanade brand with a branch also in Bangkok.

🛍️ What it is

A shopping and entertainment complex with retail shops, dining, and leisure facilities.
A key feature is the Esplanade Cineplex movie theater inside the mall, showing the latest films and entertainment.
Nearby services and leisure options typically include eateries, coffee shops, and other mall-style outlets.

📍 Location & access

Situated on Rattanathibet Road in Nonthaburi (northwest of central Bangkok).

The mall is well-known locally as Esplanade Ngamwongwan-Khae Rai, because it’s near the Ngamwongwan and Khae Rai area.

snippet.title: Visa Exempt Thailand Reductions from 60 Days to 30 Days
snippet.description:
Yes — Thailand is planning to reduce the visa‑exempt stay period for many foreign visitors. Currently, nationals of eligible countries can enter Thailand without a visa for up to 60 days for tourism purposes (often with the possibility of extending for another 30 days at immigration). However, Thai authorities have agreed “in principle” to reduce that stay to 30 days under the visa‑exemption scheme, mainly to address concerns about misuse of the longer period for illegal work or business activities. The exact date and implementation details are still being finalized.

In short:
🔹 Current situation: Visa‑free stays of up to 60 days for many passport holders.
🔹 Proposed change: Thailand intends to reduce the visa‑exempt stay to 30 days for those entries, pending final approval and announcement.
